questions.q: What does Tableau's built-in geographic hierarchy let you do?
options: Merge two unrelated data sources without a join
Drill down from a broader level (like Country) to a narrower one (like City) without building anything manually
Convert any dimension into a measure instantly
Automatically create custom sales territories for any business
questions.explain: Tableau nests recognized geographic fields (Country > State > City, etc.) so you can drill down through them on a map with no manual setup.

questions.q: Why would you need to manually assign a Geographic Role to a field?
options: A column with a non-obvious name (like Territory or Branch_Code) that actually contains geographic values might not be auto-detected by Tableau
Geographic Roles can only be assigned to measures, never dimensions
Manual assignment is required before any map can be built at all
Every geographic field always requires manual role assignment
questions.explain: Tableau auto-detects geography from common field names, but a field with an unusual name holding real city or region values may need its role assigned manually.

questions.q: Why can't Tableau's built-in geographic roles capture a company's real sales territories?
options: Tableau doesn't support any form of custom grouping
Built-in geographic roles only work for countries, never smaller regions
Real sales territories are business decisions, not official administrative boundaries, so no built-in geographic role corresponds to them
Sales territories are always identical to state boundaries
questions.explain: A company's territory boundaries (like a custom 'Northeast Region' that excludes part of a state) are business-defined, not official geography — no built-in role matches them.

questions.q: How do you build a custom territory that doesn't match any official geographic boundary?
options: Select the individual regions that make up the territory and use Group to combine them into a new dimension value
Change the Geographic Role of the field to 'Custom Territory'
Manually re-geocode every row in the data source
Custom territories are impossible to build in Tableau
questions.explain: Grouping selected regions combines them into one new business-defined value while the underlying real geography stays intact underneath.

questions.q: After grouping several states into a custom territory, what can you do with that new group?
options: Nothing — groups exist only for visual reference and can't be used in calculations
Only rename it, with no other functional capability
Filter, color, and aggregate by it just like any other dimension value, while the underlying real geography is still there
Use it exclusively on symbol maps, never on filled maps
questions.explain: A group behaves as a real dimension value once created — it can be used in filters, color encodings, and aggregations, on top of the real underlying geography.
